sentences.text: The appellants have filed this Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 09/11/2023 passed in claim case No.3943/2022 challenging the quantum of compensation there being no dispute regarding the fact of the accident and the liability of the Insurance Company.

2. The brief facts of the case are that on 11.10.2020 at around 05:30 A.M., the deceased Sunil @
Dinesh was returning from Indorama Square along with one Virusingh on his motorcycle, after purchasing vegetables from Betma Vegetable Market.

When they reached near Chaydipura Fata,
Sagore Betma Road, a car bearing registration number MP-09-CV-3668 driven by its driver in a rush and negligent manner, collided with the motorcycle of the Sunil, resulting in his death on the spot.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:21274 2 MA-1068-2024 2.1
The appellants have filed their claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the death of Sunil.
The Claims Tribunal, after considering the evidence on record, awarded compensation for loss of dependency amounting to Rs.11,42,400/-.
After awarding compensation under other heads, a total sum of Rs.13,07,400/- was granted.

3. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the compensation awarded by the Claims Tribunal is not adequate, as the income of the deceased according to the appellants was Rs.24,000/-
per month, as he was in the business of selling vegetable.

He submits that the accidental occurred Smt. Manisha vs Smt. Lakshmi W/O Akash Gupta Attorney ... on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128878192/

sentences.text: while the deceased was returning from the vegetable market after purchasing vegetables for his business.
Thus, he submits that the details of the accident themselves prove the deceased's involvement in the business and there is no reason to disbelieve the claim regarding the income of the deceased.
He, therefore, prays for the enhancement of compensation accordingly.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.3 / Insurance Company submits that the Claims Tribunal has considered the submissions of the appellants in detail in paras 25 to 27 of the impugned award.
It has been clearly recorded by the Claims Tribunal that no evidence worth mentioning has been produced by the appellants to prove the income of the deceased.

5. Heard learned counsel for the respective parties and perused the record.
6.

On perusal of the record, no concrete material has been found to NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:21274 3 MA-1068-2024 establish the claim that the deceased was earning Rs.24,000/- per month.
In such circumstances, the Claims Tribunal has rightly disbelieved this claim regarding the income of the deceased of Rs.24000/- per month.

However, it is noted that the Claims Tribunal has considered the income of the deceased as an unskilled labourer at Rs.6,500/-
per month.

The accident occurred on 11.10.2020 and as per the guidelines issued by the State Legal Services Authority, the minimum wages for unskilled labourer at the relevant time were Rs.8,400/-
per month.

7. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Hans Raj vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. passed in SLP (C)
No.3511/2020 has held that in the absence of any material regarding the income of the deceased, the guidelines issued by the State Legal Services Authority can be considered.

entities.text: Hans Raj vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, in view of the minimum wages prescribed by the State Legal Services Authority, the income of the deceased is taken as Rs.8,400/- per month.
8. As regards compensation under other heads, it is seen that the Claims Tribunal has awarded just and proper compensation.

9. After above modification, the compensation for loss of dependency would change to Rs.15,99,360/- and the total compensation would come to Rs.17,64,360/- after deducting the amount already awarded by the Claims Tribunal, which was Rs.13,07,400/-.
10. The enhanced amount would be Rs.4,56,960/- which should be paid to the appellants with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the application before the Claims Tribunal.
11. In the above terms, the appeal stands disposed of.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:21274 4 MA-1068-2024 12.
In view of the disposal of the appeal, all the pending applications are hereby closed.
